title: grap-target
desc: Shell-safe output contract for a11y find. Use when you need a paste-ready grap target that survives shell copy/paste, re-run verification, and code-review/debug workflows. Keep # FOCUS for the currently focused leaf path when interaction side effects matter, and keep # TARGET as the primary hwnd:0x... token with high-signal context for both Claude and Codex. Favor minimal operator options such as verify, review, and dry-run only when they improve safety or ambiguity.
steps: Treat a11y find as a contract for both humans and Codex: the output must be paste-ready, shell-safe, and verifiable.
Emit one shared # FOCUS line when the focused leaf may affect interaction, including modal/error popups; keep it as a full grap string in quotes.
Emit one # TARGET block per match; use {..} with hwnd first, then pid/proc, then the matching field/snippet, and quote the full grap expression so it can be pasted as one argument.
Include the matching field/snippet in a compact {match:...} section when it helps explain why this target was selected.

[v6.2+ SCORE OUTPUT] # TARGET line in find output now followed by [OK] Nms score={field:score,...} -- score for every addressable field (domain/proc/cls/title), 0..1 = pattern_literal_chars / field_value_chars. 1.00 = exact match OR un-specified candidate ready to paste into grap. <1.00 = wildcard match (less specific). Example: score={domain:1.00,proc:0.86,cls:0.54,title:0.22} tells you domain is the tightest handle, title is noisy. Use to tighten grap: any 1.00 field not yet in your grap is a precision candidate.

[v6.2+ PERF CONTRACT] find output [OK] Nms line target under 3s for most discovery calls (was 50s in v6.1). Electron (VS Code, Chrome_WidgetWin_1 + non-Chromium proc) and MFC/Afx windows (Heroes4, nkrunlite) skip UIA discovery traversal. Read-only actions use FastExit path (no TeeWriter/eye tick). When emitting target grap, remember this contract: slow find = something regressed.

PARENT CHAIN FIELDS (2026-05-18): cmd:'' forces full untruncated command line in output (commit 32958069e). ppid:N matches processes whose direct parent PID is N (e.g. {proc:'bash',ppid:180692}). ppids:[N1,N2,...] matches processes whose parent chain contains ANY listed PID -- useful for finding all bash shells under your Claude Code session: {proc:'bash',ppids:[MY_CLAUDE_PID]}. ppids:N is a single-element-list alias. ppids:'' is OUTPUT MODE: no parent-chain filter, but every match renders a one-line 'ancestors: PID(name) -> PID(name) -> ...' chain (walk up to 16 hops via GetParentProcessId; unknown names show as ?). Use ppids:'' to discover process lineage.

USAGE VERIFIED (2026-05-18): ppids:[N] filter -- {proc:'bash',ppids:[4084]} correctly matches bash whose direct parent is PID 4084. ppids:'' output -- {proc:'bash',ppids:''} prints 'ancestors: 173860(bash) -> 4084(?)' chain. ppids:N scalar -- same as ppids:[N]. NOTE: wkappbot windows only finds processes that are visible in PROC-mode scan; claude.exe child bash shells with no top-level window appear in ppids:'' output but are NOT enumerated by wkappbot windows without an explicit pid: match -- separate issue. Verified in v7.3.51.
